steps.title: Attach the product name to each order line
steps.change: The task covers products that appear on sale lines. Each detail row supplies the product ID, order ID and quantity needed to count sales.
steps.added_sql:
SELECT O.OrderDetailID, O.OrderID, O.ProductID, P.Product, O.Quantity
FROM OrderDetails AS O
LEFT JOIN Products AS P ON O.ProductID = P.ProductID
ORDER BY O.OrderDetailID;
steps.sql:
SELECT O.OrderDetailID, O.OrderID, O.ProductID, P.Product, O.Quantity
FROM OrderDetails AS O
LEFT JOIN Products AS P ON O.ProductID = P.ProductID
ORDER BY O.OrderDetailID;

steps.title: Group by product and calculate the metrics
steps.change: The metrics answer different questions. Pen's quantities add up to five. Its two lines happen to belong to different orders. If it appears again in order 10, the line count increases and the distinct order count stays at two.
steps.added_sql:
select O.ProductID,P.Product,sum (O.Quantity) as units_sold, count(OrderDetailID)  as order_lines, count(distinct(OrderID)) as orders
-- …
left join Products as P on O.ProductID =P.ProductID
group by O.ProductID
ORDER BY O.ProductID;
steps.sql:
select O.ProductID,P.Product,sum (O.Quantity) as units_sold, count(OrderDetailID)  as order_lines, count(distinct(OrderID)) as orders
from OrderDetails as O
left join Products as P on O.ProductID =P.ProductID
group by O.ProductID
ORDER BY O.ProductID;

steps.title: Apply the ranking and verify ties
steps.change: Both tables have ProductID, so qualifying the tie-breaker makes it unambiguous. Run the learner query above.
steps.added_sql: order by sum (O.Quantity) desc , O.ProductID asc
